item.title: Teignbridge Training Night
item.author: paul@insightsforaction.uk (Paul Hewson)
item.description:
This was a sunny evening, but there was a little more swell than I’d anticipated, maybe 0.5 metres.

It took a while getting on the water. There were four paddlers in the pod, one experienced paddler recovering from injury, one relatively new paddler (second time out in his sea kayak) and two novice paddlers who had done a lot of pool sessions but this was their first time on the sea. They both had second hand Dagger Approaches.

item.title: Gentle Paddle to Dawlish
item.author: paul@insightsforaction.uk (Paul Hewson)
item.description: This was a short paddle on an overcast but comfortable day. We left Teignmouth around 11am having a slow coffee at Coryton Cove and back again to Teignmouth by about 2pm.

item.title: Totnes to Kingswear
item.author: paul@insightsforaction.uk (Paul Hewson)
item.description:
Photo Credit: Fiona Hiscox Tracker

Photo Credit: Paul Hewson

Photo Credit: Paul Hewson

Photo Credit: Paul Hewson

It took about 90 minutes to arrange the car shuffle; most cars parked in Kingswear with the bare minimum returning to Totnes. We embarked from Longmarsh Car Park and followed the tide down the river. Weather was extremely cold, and it was a little windy, especially turning after Dittisham where the Dart widens out.

item.title: Maidencombe Paddle
item.author: paul@insightsforaction.uk (Paul Hewson)
item.description:
Photo Credit: Paul Hewson screenshot

This was a short but challenging paddle from Teignmouth to Maidencombe. I think the plan had been to stop in for coffee and then move on to Babbacombe for lunch, but there was a fair bit of swell. Andy Benham suggested it was closer to 1m than the 0.8 shown on my forecast.
